newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault studies sale of wiring division.
newsitem.headline: Renault studies sale of wiring division.

text.p: French carmaker Renault SA said on Wednesday that it was studying the sale of its wiring division to Sylea, a subsidiary of the Labinal group.

Renault said it was reviewing the terms of a partnership with Sylea involving three industrial sites, Dreux Cablage, wholly-owned unit Renault Industrie Maroc (RIM) and 66.2 percent owned Renault Industrie Tunisie (RIT).
Under the terms, Dreux would be transformed into a subsidiary in mid-1997 to create a holding company for the three plants, each of which employs around 450 people.

Sylea would take a 49 percent stake in the holding company before the end of June 1997 and would have an option to buy the remaining 51 percent before the end of 1998, Renault said in a statement. Terms were not disclosed.

Renault said the project would allow it to confirm the selection of Dreux, RIT and RIM to develop the wiring for two major vehicle projects which would maintain the current level of activity at the three plants for the next five years at least.

The project would also enable it to "reduce the cost of wiring, the second-largest cost item in a vehicle after the power unit, thanks to the technical potential and sheer size of its partner, specialised in this field of activity."
It said Sylea, which generated 4.2 billion francs in sales in 1995, was ranked second in the European wiring market with a 14 percent share.
Renault said the wiring industry was characterised by increased specialisation, falling prices and rising research expenses.
"In this context Renault will no longer be able by itself to finance the engineering work and volumes required to develop its wiring division," it said.
It said the staff councils of Sylea and Renault would be consulted about the partnership on October 29.
